observation_summary: The compiler's function inliner was performing an optimization that incorrectly reordered operations, leading to incorrect evaluation order when a function body had side effects and arguments could be side-effected.
reasoning_summary: The fix introduces a conditional check (`if (hasSideEffects && NodeUtil.canBeSideEffected(cArg))`) to prevent inlining when the function body has side effects and the arguments are susceptible to being side-effected. This is a classic guard/validation logic correction to ensure the safety of an optimization, fitting the 'Checking' category.
evidence_used: The fix adds a conditional check: 'if (hasSideEffects && NodeUtil.canBeSideEffected(cArg)) { return CanInlineResult.NO; }'
The bug report describes an erroneous optimization where the compiler incorrectly reordered operations, failing to account for side effects.
The fix logic validates the safety of the inlining operation based on side-effect conditions.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the inlining logic is a method, the root cause is the absence of a safety check (guard) to prevent the optimization under specific conditions, which is the definition of Checking.
